response.evidence: Counts are approximate, from a manual review of the rows. Asian Male applicants were denied about 15 times out of roughly 170 applications, a denial rate near 9%. White Male (about 14 denials out of roughly 200, near 7%) and White applicants overall (about 7-8%) are similar, and Asian Female, Hispanic and Joint groups show comparable or higher rates. The small gap is within what chance and differences in financial profile could explain. About half of the Asian Male denials had a debt-to-income ratio of 50% or higher, and high-DTI applications are denied across every race. One pattern merits caution: Asian Male applicants with 50-60% DTI were all denied (0 of 6 approved), while White Male applicants in that band were mostly approved (5 of 6). However, those approved White Male applicants mostly had low loan-to-value ratios (about 37-59%, with one at 100%). The denied Asian Male applicants mostly had LTVs of 67-92%, so the difference is confounded by LTV and the sample is very small. A few denials with otherwise moderate profiles appear across all races, including White Male, and suggest factors not captured here, such as credit score. This dataset lacks credit history and other underwriting variables. It shows no clear statistical disparity against Asian males, and it cannot determine whether any individual decision was discriminatory.
